solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lack of progress from unruly antagonist

indicators.note: something unruly will not stay in order, so the letters of the next word get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A troublesome opponent is holding up a team's advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antagonist' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is simply the raw letters for STAGNATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the state of being stuck, with no growth, development or forward movement.

clue.text: It is included in the tax

indicators.note: something included in another thing sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written; it forms the outside
taken as written; it goes inside

explanation.surface: A grumble that some charge is buried within the overall tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: TH(IT)E. The whole clue reads like plain prose, but it splits into tiny pieces. A tithe was a tenth of income paid to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a levy, historically one tenth of produce or earnings given to support the church.

clue.text: Explosive anger possibly ends in wild dispute

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the collected letters run riot into a new order
possibly hints that the word is one arrangement among many that its letters could form

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its very first and very last letters, nothing between

parts.note: the opening and closing letters of dispute

explanation.surface: A furious row ends in a wild argument that blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGER plus D and E, the ends of 'dispute', are rearranged to GRENADE. 'Explosive' is a noun here, as in a device.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, so it is an example of an explosive device.

clue.text: Fat cats oddly ignored decree from parliament

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions leaves only the second, fourth and sixth characters

parts.note: the even letters of the two words read together; that the letters also run backwards across the words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Wealthy bigwigs paid no attention to a law passed by the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat cats are rich, powerful people, which makes 'ignored' sound like part of the story rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a law passed by the legislature, so a parliamentary decree is an act.

clue.text: Resolute aim to get hold of family member

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: an aim is an intent or purpose
short for sister

explanation.surface: A determined goal of keeping a relative close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family member' could be many relatives; the short informal sister is the one that fits, held inside the word for aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent keeps demanding something firmly and will not give way, which is being resolute.

clue.text: Northern Ireland, Germany, and another country

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Northern Ireland
short form of Germany

explanation.surface: A list of places that reads like a geography quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: The list looks like three separate countries; the first two simply supply abbreviations for the third, a West African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African nation, so it is one more country to add to the list.

clue.text: Scoff at extremely dire rollercoaster?

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last characters

parts.note: first and last letters of dire
a rollercoaster is a fairground ride; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Mocking a theme park attraction as truly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as an intensifier for 'dire', but it selects that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule something with contempt, the same as scoffing at it.

clue.text: Second grade in a trial, ideally

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other words that follow

parts.note: a trial is a test
B is the second grade after A

explanation.surface: A mark of B awarded in an exam, which is the most one could hope for.
explanation.walkthrough: A T(B)EST: the grade goes inside the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the most favourable circumstances, or under perfect conditions, much as ideally does.

clue.text: Gents at sea capturing one small seal

indicators.note: capturing something means enclosing it, so the rearranged letters surround another piece
at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Sailors grabbing a young seal pup from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal in this nautical scene, but it is the stamp pressed into wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small official stamp, often set in a ring, used to impress wax on documents.

clue.text: Awesome, ace, flawless person making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so these letters travel back the way they came

parts.note: A is the card symbol for an ace
someone wonderful is called a gem

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant, perfect star returning to form.
explanation.walkthrough: A then GEM is written backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for great or tremendous, an informal synonym for awesome.

clue.text: Have a siesta, then shower? Check!

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon rest
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: Someone ticking off a holiday to-do list: nap, then wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests washing, but it is weather; 'Check!' looks like a tick on the list, not a verb meaning hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, which is a synonym of restrain.

clue.text: Nasty sort starts to drink all my port

parts.note: a rotter is an old-fashioned word for a nasty person

indicators.note: the starts of several words are their opening characters, one from each

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A cad helps themselves to the whole bottle of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' sounds like the wine a rotter might drink, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam in the Netherlands is one of the largest seaports in Europe, so it is an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Periodic payment given by father and mother, maybe

parts.note: an informal word for father
rent is paid at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Mum and dad help with the monthly bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given by' puts the payment beside the father, so PA comes first. 'Father and mother' looks like the definition but the answer is singular; only 'mother, maybe' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a parent, hence the 'maybe' signalling an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: A minor thoroughfare in Europe, say

parts.note: taken as written
British roads are graded, and the lettered grade below the main routes marks minor ones

explanation.surface: Describing a quiet back road on a European holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A roads are main routes, B roads are minor ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in Europe, from a British viewpoint, is an example of being overseas in a foreign country.

clue.text: Some slides aren't about to get destroyed

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the run of letters is read from right to left
some means only part, so the letters sit inside a longer run of the clue

parts.note: the end of slides and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A presenter's slideshow is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span 'sliDES AREn't' and are then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erased has been wiped out completely, leaving no trace, which is what destroyed means.

clue.text: A group of words said to indicate breaches of the peace

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want what the phrase sounds like rather than its spelling

parts.note: a phrase is a group of words

explanation.surface: Someone choosing the right expression for public disturbances.
explanation.walkthrough: An affray is the legal term in Britain for fighting in a public place.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrays are public brawls that frighten bystanders, a type of breach of the peace in law.

clue.text: Defensive equipment meant to be deployed by a group of soldiers

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: deploying troops spreads them out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Royal Marines
taken as written

explanation.surface: Weapons intended for use by a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deployed' fits the military picture but is the anagram signal; RM is the usual abbreviation for the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: Armament means weapons and military equipment collectively, the means by which a force defends itself.

clue.text: Complete collection of books set aside

parts.note: complete as in the whole
the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full library set reserved for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection of books' suggests a library, but the setter means the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or earmark a share for a particular purpose, which is setting it aside.

clue.text: Swimmer flagging at the outset, kind of

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening character is kept

parts.note: first letter of flagging
the informal suffix meaning somewhat or sort of

explanation.surface: A swimmer tiring at the start of a race, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' reads as a person in the water; here it is a creature that lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is an animal that lives and moves through water, so it is the archetypal swimmer.

clue.text: Unseemly outburst is noticed on a podcast

indicators.note: a podcast is heard rather than read, so only the sound of the word matters

parts.note: noticed means observed

explanation.surface: A presenter's embarrassing tantrum gets spotted by listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a scene is to cause a public fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a noisy public display of temper or emotion, an embarrassing outburst.

clue.text: Slow song from fancy dance promo

parts.note: a ball is a formal, elegant dance
a promo is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A smoochy number taken from a dance-party advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a sentimental song, typically slow and romantic in modern pop music.

clue.text: Last bit of orange put in port? Bliss!

indicators.note: putting something in another places it inside that word

parts.note: a haven is a harbour

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final character

parts.note: final letter of orange

explanation.surface: Adding a twist of orange peel to a glass of port: sheer joy.
explanation.walkthrough: H(E)AVEN: the E slots in after the first letter of the harbour. 'Port' suggests the drink, but here it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is a state of supreme happiness, so bliss and heaven are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of the wall fell

indicators.note: part of means only a portion, so the letters lie within a longer stretch of the clue

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A section of the wall collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the verb meaning to cut down a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it down, and hew means to chop or cut with an axe.

clue.text: Teams write about something unproductive

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Teams writing about a pointless task.
explanation.definitionFit: A time-waster is an activity that consumes hours without achieving anything useful or worthwhile.
